We need to identify topology of subnetwork 2 between nodes X1 and X2 given measurements between nodes N_b1, N_b2, X1, X2. There are three resistors total. Likely a triangle (delta) between N_b1, N_b2, and X1? Actually measurements: N_b1-N_b2 =15, N_b1-X1=10, N_b1-X2=35, N_b2-X1=25, N_b2-X2=20, X1-X2=45. That's six pairwise resistances among four nodes. With three resistors, the network must be a tree (no loops) because three resistors connecting four nodes yields a tree (no cycles). In a tree, resistance between any two nodes is sum of resistors along unique path. So we can try to assign three resistors connecting nodes in some configuration that yields those pairwise resistances.

We have nodes: N_b1, N_b2, X1, X2. Three resistors: likely R1 between N_b1 and N_b2? That would give 15 directly. Then other two resistors connect maybe N_b1 to X1 (10) and N_b2 to X2 (20) etc. Let's test: Suppose R_ab =15 (N_b1-N_b2). R1 =10 (N_b1-X1). R2 =20 (N_b2-X2). Then compute other distances: N_b1-X2 path: N_b1-N_b2 (15)+R2 (20)=35 matches measurement 35. N_b2-X1 path: N_b2-N_b1 (15)+R1 (10)=25 matches measurement 25. X1-X2 path: X1-N_b1 (10)+N_b1-N_b2 (15)+N_b2-X2 (20)=45 matches measurement 45. All match! So topology is a simple series tree: N_b1 connected to N_b2 (R12=15), N_b1 to X1 (R13=10), N_b2 to X2 (R24=20). That's three resistors.

Thus output JSON: resistors mapping names to values, connections list of [node1,node2, resistorName].

We need naming: R1, R2, R3 left to right? Not sure but we can assign R1 = 10 (N_b1-X1), R2 = 15 (N_b1-N_b2), R3 = 20 (N_b2-X2). Provide.
